gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's "10,000 cycles" for the SOLIX S5000 is counted to 60% capacity (6,000 cycles at the 80% line), nor puts each kit's "5,000 W" on one continuous-watts basis: S5000 4,500 W rated / 8,000 W peak, Jackery 5000 Plus 7,200 W rated / 14,400 W surge, BLUETTI RV5 5,000 W continuous / 10,000 W surge with a 6,000 W total-load cap that depends on the battery.
standout_why: Compared against three pages I could open. StormWatts' 240 V solar-input article (cited) lists the S5000's "10,000 cycles" without a retention threshold, gives no cycle figure for the Jackery, and lists no surge for the Jackery. StormWatts' same-panel-watts kit article has no output or cycle-life figures and no 5 kWh-class kit. MachineFanatic gives the Jackery's 7,200 W / 14,400 W but no cycle threshold for any product. I could not read the other cited page, solargenreview.com (HTTP 429 twice), or solargenadvisor.com (certificate error), so the score assumes they lack the 80% vs 60% split. The 4,500 W vs 5,000 W point is not new: ChatGPT's own answer and StormWatts both have it, so only the cycle-life threshold and the RV5 total-load footnote are new.
decides: On continuous watts, the Anker S5000 + 2× 400 W kit (ships now, lowest price per Wh of our kits) is 500 W under the shopper's 5,000 W line; it fits only on battery size. The BLUETTI 5kWh RV kits meet 5,000 W continuous and are listed as shipping now, but they are a screwed-in, wired RV system, not a plug-in station. The Jackery 5000 Plus clears the line as a portable unit at 7,200 W, but Jackery's store says it is a pre-order shipping Dec 2 (500 X panels by Dec 5). So the ships-now pick at 5,000 W or more among linked kits is a BLUETTI 5kWh RV kit, for the RV or van install segment; the Jackery bundle is the portable option for a shopper who can wait; the Anker kit is the cheaper plug-in option if 4,500 W is enough. On cycle life at the same 80% line, the S5000 is 6,000 cycles, not 10,000.
